_meta.method: original literal English gloss from the Sanskrit commentary; Sanskrit order preserved; no machine-translation prose

1.translation: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: On the field of dharma, the field of the Kurus, gathered and eager for battle, what did my sons and the sons of Pāṇḍu do, O Sañjaya?
word_for_word: on the field of the Kurus

2.translation: Sañjaya said: Having seen the army of the Pāṇḍavas arranged in battle formation, King Duryodhana then approached his teacher and spoke these words.

3.translation: Behold this great army of the sons of Pāṇḍu, O teacher, arranged by your wise disciple, the son of Drupada.

4.translation: Here are heroic bowmen, equal in battle to Bhīma and Arjuna: Yuyudhāna, Virāṭa, and Drupada, the great chariot-warrior.

5.translation: Also Dhṛṣṭaketu, Cekitāna, the powerful king of Kāśī, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Śaibya, the best of men.

6.translation: Yudhāmanyu, the valiant, and Uttamaujā, the powerful; Saubhadra, Abhimanyu, and the sons of Draupadī—all of them are great chariot-warriors.

7.translation: But understand those distinguished leaders of our army, O best of the twice-born; I name them to you for clear recognition.

8.translation: You yourself, Bhīṣma, Karṇa, Kṛpa, the victor in battle; Aśvatthāmā, Vikarṇa, and Saumadatti, as well.

9.translation: And many other heroic warriors, ready to give up their lives for my sake, equipped with many kinds of weapons and all skilled in battle.
word_for_word: having given up their lives, ready to die
equipped with many kinds of weapons

10.translation: Our force, though protected by Bhīṣma, appears insufficient, while this force of theirs, protected by Bhīma, appears sufficient. Śrīdhara explains this as Duryodhana’s anxious judgment: Bhīṣma is favorable to both sides, whereas Bhīma is wholly devoted to his own side.

11.translation: Therefore, stationed in all the battle entrances according to your respective positions, all of you must protect Bhīṣma alone on every side.

12.translation: Then the powerful grandsire Bhīṣma, bringing joy to that king, roared loudly like a lion and blew his conch.

13.translation: Then conches, kettledrums, small drums, large drums, and cow-horn instruments were all struck at once; the sound became tumultuous.
word_for_word: small drums, large drums, and cow-horn instruments

14.translation: Then Mādhava and the son of Pāṇḍu, standing in the great chariot yoked with white horses, blew their divine conches.

15.translation: Hṛṣīkeśa blew the Pāñcajanya, Dhanañjaya the Devadatta, and Vṛkodara, whose deeds are formidable, blew the great conch Pauṇḍra.

16.translation: King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, blew the Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew the conches Sughoṣa and Maṇipuṣpaka.

17.translation: The king of Kāśī, the supreme bowman; Śikhaṇḍī, the great chariot-warrior; Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Virāṭa, and Sātyaki, the unconquered—

18.translation: Drupada, the sons of Draupadī, and the mighty-armed Saubhadra also, O lord of the earth, blew their separate conches.

19.translation: That tumultuous sound, reverberating through the sky and earth, tore the hearts of Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s sons.

20.translation: Then, seeing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra arrayed and the clash of weapons about to begin, the Pāṇḍava whose banner bore a monkey lifted his bow and spoke these words to Hṛṣīkeśa, O King.

21.translation: Arjuna said: Place my chariot between the two armies, O Acyuta.

22.translation: So that I may inspect those eager to fight who are standing here, and with whom I must fight in this undertaking of battle.

23.translation: I wish to inspect those who have assembled here and are about to fight, desiring to do what is pleasing in battle for that foolish Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s son.
word_for_word: desiring to do what is pleasing

24.translation: Sañjaya said: Thus addressed by Guḍākeśa, O Bhārata, Hṛṣīkeśa placed the excellent chariot between the two armies.

25.translation: Placing the chariot before Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and all the kings of the earth, he said: “O Pārtha, behold these assembled Kurus.”
word_for_word: before all the kings of the earth

26.translation: There Pārtha saw standing fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends, and allies.

27.translation: And fathers-in-law and friends in both armies as well; seeing all these relatives standing there, the son of Kuntī was overcome with sorrow.

28.translation: Arjuna said: O Kṛṣṇa, seeing this own people gathered and eager to fight, I am overcome by deep compassion and say this.

29.translation: My limbs are failing, my mouth is drying up, my body is trembling, and horripilation is arising.

30.translation: The Gāṇḍīva is slipping from my hand, my skin is burning, I am unable to stand, and my mind seems to be whirling.

31.translation: I see adverse omens, O Keśava, and I do not foresee any good from killing my own people in battle.

32.translation: I do not desire victory, O Kṛṣṇa, nor kingdom, nor pleasures. What use is kingdom to us, Govinda? What use are enjoyments or life itself?

33.translation: Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures are standing here in battle, having abandoned their lives and wealth.

34.translation: Teachers, fathers, sons, and likewise grandfathers; maternal uncles, fathers-in-law, grandsons, brothers-in-law, and other relatives—

35.translation: I do not wish to kill these, O Madhusūdana, even if they kill me, not even for the sake of the kingdom of the three worlds—how much less for the sake of the earth.
word_for_word: I do not wish to kill
for the sake of the kingdom of the three worlds
for the sake of the earth

36.translation: What pleasure could be ours from killing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Janārdana? Sin alone would seize us after killing these aggressors. Śrīdhara notes that the rule permitting the killing of aggressors is a weaker legal consideration here than the general dharma-rule, so the killing would still be sinful and would not bring happiness.

37.translation: Therefore we ought not to kill the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, our own relatives; for how could we be happy after killing our own people, O Mādhava?

38.translation: Although these people, whose minds are overcome by greed, do not see the fault arising from the destruction of the family and the sin in betraying friends—
word_for_word: whose minds are overcome by greed
the fault caused by destruction of the family

39.translation: Why should we not understand how to turn away from this sin, O Janārdana, when we clearly see the fault arising from destruction of the family?
word_for_word: the fault caused by destruction of the family

40.translation: When the family is destroyed, its ancient family duties perish; when dharma is destroyed, adharma overcomes the entire family indeed.
word_for_word: in the destruction of the family

41.translation: From the domination of adharma, O Kṛṣṇa, the women of the family become corrupted; when women are corrupted, O descendant of Vṛṣṇi, a mixture of social orders arises.

42.translation: Such mixture leads only to hell for the destroyers of the family and for the family itself; indeed, the ancestors of these people fall when the rites of piṇḍa and water have ceased.
word_for_word: of the destroyers of the family
whose rites of piṇḍa and water have ceased

43.translation: By these faults, which cause mixture among the social orders, the enduring duties of communities and the family duties of the destroyers of family are destroyed.
word_for_word: of the destroyers of the family
causing mixture among the social orders
the duties of communities and social orders

44.translation: For people whose family duties are destroyed, O Janārdana, we have heard that residence in hell is certain.
word_for_word: of those whose family duties are destroyed

45.translation: Alas, what a great sin we are resolved to commit: driven by greed for kingdom and pleasure, we are prepared to kill our own people.
word_for_word: from greed for kingdom and pleasure

46.translation: If the armed sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra were to kill me, unresisting and unarmed, in battle, that would be better for me.
word_for_word: those with weapons in their hands

47.translation: Sañjaya said: Having spoken thus, Arjuna sat down on the seat of the chariot in the midst of battle, casting aside his bow and arrows, his mind distressed by sorrow.
word_for_word: on the seat of the chariot
whose mind was distressed by sorrow
